status: DIAGNOSED - NOT FIXED. Every candidate fix changes R2 inputs and therefore production behaviour.
authority: CEO decision required. Same class as the deferred SECTOR-1/SECTOR-2 items.

findings.title: Every 200-day feature is structurally impossible
findings.what: adapt_prices(lookback_days=90). No caller overrides it, so the canonical bar set is 90 rows per symbol.

evidence.note: The builder's own guard `if len(closes) >= 200` is correct. It never fires because it is handed 90 bars.

findings.refutes: An insufficient-history explanation. The parquets hold roughly 1,300 bars; the truncation is the adapter's.

findings.title: Historical replay windows shrink to zero as the as_of recedes
findings.what: `df.tail(lookback_days)` is applied BEFORE the `cutoff` filter. The last 90 rows of the FILE are taken first, then anything after the as_of is dropped - so a past-dated request keeps only the overlap.
findings.consequence: Past-dated feature computation degrades silently and returns NOTHING beyond roughly four months. No error is raised.
findings.significance: This is the mechanical explanation for the BLOCKED-INSUFFICIENT HISTORY verdict returned by every historical R3 wave. The constraint was read as a data-depth limit; it is an ordering defect in one line.

findings.title: Sector relatives are empty in BOTH markets, independent of the India sector defect
findings.what: USA carries a sector label for all 516 names yet sector_rank, sector_return_1m_pct, sector_is_leader and sector_is_laggard are 0% populated. So the sector-relative computation fails for a reason separate from SECTOR-1, which is about India's missing labels.

production_impact.reasoning: These columns are null for EVERY ticker, not a subset. trend.py adds 0.15*s200.fillna(0) and sector_rotation.py resolves to score 0 / confidence 0 for the whole universe, so the effect is a constant offset rather than a per-ticker distortion. Relative ranking on a given day is therefore intact.
what_is_genuinely_lost: sector_rotation contributes nothing at all: score 0 and confidence 0 for every name, so one of eleven models is inert.
momentum carries a 0.10 weight on price_above_sma200 that can never fire.
trend's score magnitude is deflated by up to 0.15 for every name, which matters wherever an ABSOLUTE threshold is applied rather than a rank.
trend's confidence counts only adx and s50, so it does not report the missing s200 - the model looks more confident than its inputs justify.

explicitly_not_done: No fix applied. Raising lookback_days or reordering tail/cutoff would populate sma_200 and the sector relatives, which changes momentum, trend and sector_rotation inputs and therefore R2 scoring.
No rejected research family reopened. Whether prior MA200 and peer/sector rejections were decided against structurally empty columns is a question for the CEO, not a licence to re-run them.
No threshold, weight, gate or eligibility rule touched.
recommended_sequence_if_authorised: 1. Fix CANON-2 alone (cutoff before tail). It is the historical-replay blocker and does NOT change today's live window, which already ends at the as_of.
2. Re-measure how far back replay can actually reach once the ordering is correct.
3. Treat CANON-1 separately. Raising the window DOES change live R2 inputs and needs its own authorisation and a before/after decision diff.
